what_this_is: The register of suppliers who asked to SEE a private preview and have granted PlotNua nothing. One row per supplier, read by atlas-tools/prove-preview-only-containment.mjs. Adding a supplier here is what puts their preview under containment; it is not a permission of any kind.
why_a_register_rather_than_a_script_each: The first two of these -- Cosy Cabins and Irish Sauna Company -- were about to get a second near-identical proof file. Three would have guaranteed that a fix applied to one was forgotten in the others. The checks live in one place and this file is the only thing that changes per supplier.
the_rule_these_rows_enforce: UNKNOWN is not GRANTED. A supplier in this register has replied PREVIEW, not YES. Their preview page carries their published FACTS, with attribution and a link back. Whether it may also carry their IMAGERY is decided by imagery_mode, and by nothing else.
imagery_mode: Required on every row, and an unrecognised value is an ERROR rather than a pass. 'none' is the default case: the supplier granted nothing at all, so none of their imagery may appear on ANY page, including their own preview. 'preview-only' is the narrower case where the supplier invited imagery for the preview in writing while withholding publication: their imagery may appear on their own preview page and NOWHERE else, a preview-scoped row must exist in image-rights-records.json carrying that invitation, and that row's conditions must name the page. The two modes are checked by different code paths on purpose -- a 'none' supplier must never pass through the 'preview-only' branch because somebody edited one character.
the_grant_boundary: A supplier with a full publication grant does not belong in this register at all; they live only in image-rights-records.json. A 'preview-only' supplier appears in BOTH, and that is the one case where both is correct: the rights row is what lets the gate pass the preview, and this register is what stops the row reaching anything else.

graduated_to_full_grant.name: Irish Sauna Company
graduated_to_full_grant.was: imagery_mode 'none' — they had replied PREVIEW on 2 October 2026 and granted nothing.
graduated_to_full_grant.why_removed: Brona replied on 9 October 2026 at 12:02 UTC from info@irishsaunacompany.com, Gmail thread 1a0fd83ddde922b1: “we would be delighted for you to use our imagery and product on your site.” That is a full publication grant, not an invitation to show imagery on a preview, so under this register's own rule (see 'the_grant_boundary') the row does not belong here any more. Containment by ABSENCE is the wrong instrument for a supplier who has said yes: keeping the row at imagery_mode 'none' would have asserted in the repository that they granted nothing, which is now false.
graduated_to_full_grant.what_constrains_them_now: image-rights-records.json and the generated manifest, organisation_record recLW0vZbkBGPRkZ9, permitted_domain irishsaunacompany.com, required_credit © Irish Sauna Company. atlas-tools/validate-image-rights.js refuses any image of theirs from another host, and refuses all of them if the credit leaves the page. irish-sauna-company-preview.html was retired on 27 Oct 2026 (it described the withdrawn Harvia range). Since 27 Oct 2026 the grant is exercised on the Garden Retreat maker explorer for the eight enumerated Island Collection product visualisations only (atlas-tools/build-irish-sauna-company-collection-record.py).

graduated_to_full_grant.name: OGNYX
graduated_to_full_grant.was: imagery_mode 'preview-only' -- four images invited for ognyx-preview.html while publication was withheld.
graduated_to_full_grant.why_removed: OGNYX answered the 12 October 2026 ask to "feature OGNYX and use the selected product images shown there" with "We have reviewed your offer and can confirm we would be happy to proceed with this" (13 Oct 2026, Gmail 1a13699d55beb7f9). The founder decided on 14 October 2026 to proceed on those words. That is a publication grant, so under this register's own rule (the_grant_boundary) the row does not belong here any more.
graduated_to_full_grant.what_constrains_them_now: image-rights-records.json (approved_assets: exactly four images, by enumeration) and atlas-tools/prove-ognyx-imagery-containment.mjs, which refuses any other OGNYX image on any page and requires the credit, the link back and the visualisation labels wherever one appears. The publication gate derives PUBLISHABLE on evidence, with no founder exception.

suppliers.forbidden_claims_note: MONEY AND SERVICE AREA, not product facts. Switch Electrical's own homepage says "cut your electricity bills" and carries three customer reviews mentioning bill reductions; that is their copy about their customers and would be an unevidenced claim about a stranger's house in PlotNua's voice. The service-area bans exist because the site names five counties and adds "across Leinster" -- a page that rounded that up to nationwide would send them enquiries they cannot serve. NOTE WHAT IS NOT BANNED: the words "free" and "guarantee". The free survey, the free quote and the free BER are all published, and the Clean Export Guarantee is the name of a real scheme.
suppliers.evidence: Switch Electrical replied "Preview pls" on 5 October 2026 to outreach sent to sales@switchelectrical.ie, when the outreach offered both YES and PREVIEW. A request to see the page is not a grant.
suppliers.atlas_permission_ref: NOT IN ATLAS — Switch Electrical Limited has no organisation record, no product record and no permission record. A full-tree search on 5 October 2026 returned nothing. There is no relationship to reflect and none is implied.

suppliers.name: Sauna Experts

image_hosts.why: their WordPress media library on their own domain, which is where every product and gallery image is served from

suppliers.forbidden_claims_note: BORROWED SUPERLATIVES FIRST. Their own site calls them "Ireland's Number One Sauna Shop", "the highest rated sauna supplier in Ireland", "Ireland's Top Sauna Manufacturer" and "the most professional". Those are their marketing and nobody's verified fact; PlotNua repeating one would convert an unchecked claim into an apparent ranking on a page whose whole purpose is to show editorial independence. THE EXPERIENCE FIGURES ARE BANNED BECAUSE THEY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER: the homepage says "over 20 years of experience" of the custom saunas and, four paragraphs later, "over 16 years" of the founders. Both are first-party and they disagree, so neither is used. NOTE WHAT IS NOT BANNED: installation and nationwide delivery. Unlike the Irish Sauna Company case, this supplier publishes both on the product page itself -- "nationwide delivery, sauna installation, and comprehensive support with building advisory" -- so they are evidenced and may be reported, with the open question of what sits inside the price left open rather than answered.
suppliers.evidence: Sauna Experts replied "PREVIEW" on 5 October 2026 to outreach sent to saunaexpertsltd@gmail.com, when the outreach offered both YES and PREVIEW. A request to see the page is not a grant.

The configurator's starting prices (Barrel €3,300, Cube €3,200, Hot Tub €2,300, Plunge €1,100, Phytosauna €2,100) disagree with the same site's SEO pages (from €2,800 / €3,100 / €1,950), so the page shows the configurator's figures labelled as such and asks which is right. The site carries customer quotes, a templated '15 installations in <county>' line, health claims and a statement that garden saunas are generally exempt from planning; none is verified and none may appear. Origin is not established (a separate Estonian Ecosauna Project OÜ exists), so no origin claim. NOTE WHAT IS NOT BANNED: the 32-county delivery coverage, which is published by EcoSauna and appears only attributed in their name; 'nationwide' unattributed is banned.
